results.reason: Issue 3 says the First Supplement (Sept 14) window ran Sept 28 without termination. Under §5.7(c), the Ferrovane §§4.7/4.8 inaccuracies are therefore deemed cured for Article IX and §7.2(a), and termination is waived. Buyer has no indemnity for the loss.

Issue 4 contrasts the Escrow 'actual out-of-pocket' definition (excluding diminution in value, lost profits and attorneys' fees) with the SPA definition. It explains that SPA §11.11 lets the Escrow Agreement control disbursement mechanics, which limits escrow recovery.

Issue 1 identifies the MSA §14.2 >50% deemed assignment requiring consent, triggered by the 100% purchase. It notes the consent is not in Annex 7.2(d) or covered by §7.2(d) or §5.3, so Buyer faces termination or List Price repricing after closing. The response does not use the words 'sole-source', but the 85% requirements dependence conveys the same point.
States the 10-Business-Day period ran on September 28, after September 14 delivery, before the October 13 letter.
States the escrow is $4.85M, which equals $4,850,000.
The response is a memorandum to [Partner]. Each issue gives a 'Where' location with document and section, explains why it matters, and recommends a fix.
Section 3 lists 'Things I could not resolve from the documents'. Section 4, 'Needed from the client', and the per-issue client input items flag further open points.
The response treats the Ferrovane termination right as waived and the window as expired, not as live.
Expressly states Annex 7.2(d) lists only the lender payoff and lien release, so the Tavinor consent is not a condition.
